1. The animation compares one month of renting with the first month of owning, using an illustrative character named Nina. She stands between an apartment building tagged "RENT 5%" and a house. A short stack of gold bars is labeled "rent". A much taller stack is labeled "buyer's first month". The caption cites FHFA home prices, BLS rents and Freddie Mac rates. It also says "illustrative", "US only" and "history, not a forecast".

2. In frames 1 and 2 the scene is a street of houses, with Nina at "the end of the street" and the label "Nina's month: no house yet". By frame 3 the camera has moved in and the two stacks appear, with the buyer's stack far taller than the rent stack. Frames 4 and 5 add the text "September 2026 average: 6.86%", which is the mortgage rate. Frame 6 adds "buyer's first month: $2,933". The stacks themselves don't change after frame 3. Only the text labels are added.

3. It means that, in this illustration, the first month of owning costs a lot more than a month of rent. The figure is $2,933 at a 6.86% mortgage rate. The stack heights show the gap, and "RENT 5%" presumably refers to rent growth.

4. A viewer would probably take away that buying costs noticeably more per month than renting at current rates. I can't see any explicit recommendation. The animation never says whether to rent or buy.

5. The advice in 4 is my own inference. The animation shows the cost gap in its picture and numbers, but it gives no instruction. Its "history, not a forecast" and "illustrative" labels also warn against treating it as a prediction. It also doesn't say what the $2,933 includes, so I can't tell from this image whether it covers interest, tax, insurance and repairs.
